title: Value Portrait: Assessing Language Models’ Values through Psychometrically and Ecologically Valid Items

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting the model with male and female personas and comparing its resulting Schwartz value orientation scores on the Value Portrait benchmark against real human data from the European Social Survey to identify stereotypical exaggerations.
Prompting the model with different age group personas and comparing the generated value orientation patterns against actual human age-related value trends to detect misrepresentations.
Prompting the model with left-wing and right-wing personas to measure if the model exaggerates value differences between political orientations compared to actual human data.
Prompting the model with personas of varying educational attainments (e.g., high school, bachelor's, master's) and comparing the resulting value orientation scores against human baseline data.

Prompting the model with different religious personas (e.g., Atheist, Hindu, Jewish, Muslim, Protestant) and measuring the impact on value orientation scores, such as Tradition, compared to human baselines.
Prompting the model with different racial and ethnic identities (Asian, Black, Hispanic, White) and evaluating the resulting value orientations on the Value Portrait benchmark.
Prompting the model with different income level personas (<30k, 30k-100k, 100k+) and evaluating the resulting differences in value orientation scores.
